findings.detail: All three new rows in the Closed table (lines 50, 51, 52) carry byte-identical 'Fixed by' text describing the `alignBatchResults` numeric-translation change — which is TD-042's fix only. So the register now claims TD-039 ("same red invalid badge for a stale model list") was fixed by accepting finite numbers as translations, and that TD-041 ("a model fallback is surfaced in Translate only") was too. Neither is true: TD-039 was fixed by the `no-model` state in `verifyGeminiKey` plus the blue badge in `ApiKeyModal`, and TD-041 by `advancePastRetiredModel` + the `onNotice` parameter on all four entry points. This defeats the exact purpose the register serves — the commit messages in this PR are careful about the why, and the durable artifact a future reader will actually query now gives the wrong answer for two of three entries.
findings.summary: TD-039 and TD-041 closed rows record TD-042's fix, not their own

findings.detail: The whole point of the `no-model` state is that the wording carries the diagnosis — 'Key OK', not red, plus a help line telling the user not to rotate the key and naming the script to run. But the badge (line 93) and the help block (lines 108–112) render conditionally with no `role="status"` and no `aria-live` region, so a screen-reader user who activates the Test button hears nothing at all: focus stays on the button, and the result appears silently elsewhere in the dialog. That is worse here than for the pre-existing valid/invalid/quota badges, because this state's entire value is a sentence of guidance the user has no reason to go hunting for. Low rather than medium because the information is present and reachable by re-reading the dialog; it would be medium if the button became disabled or focus moved on completion.
findings.summary: New no-model status badge and help text are not announced to screen readers

findings.detail: When TD-039 moved to the Closed table its description lost the escape on a pipe: it now ends at ``returns `'valid' \`` and the rest — ``| 'invalid' \| 'quota'`, so when the candidate walk falls off the end of `MODEL_CANDIDATES.fast`...`` — is gone. The trailing `\ ` followed by ` | ` closes the cell early, the code span is left unclosed, and the row renders with a dangling backslash where the explanation used to be. The entry that motivated the headline change in this PR is now the one entry that no longer says what it was about.
findings.summary: TD-039's Description cell is truncated mid-sentence and breaks the table row

findings.detail: The test `generateText tells its caller — Support Chat` proves the parameter is threaded through `generateText`, which it is. But `generateText`'s only production caller is `components/SupportChat.tsx:448`, `aiService.generateText(prompt, 'fast')` — no `onNotice`. So Support Chat is still the one surface where a request that quietly moved to a weaker model produces nothing but a `console.warn`, which is the precise condition TD-041 describes and which the register now marks closed. The commit message is honest about this (it claims Web Scraper, Compare and OCR only); the test name and the register's closure are not. A test whose name asserts a wiring that does not exist is the kind that stays green while the gap it names reopens.
findings.summary: Test named for Support Chat, but Support Chat still does not pass onNotice
